answer: Each agent claims an orchard turnout on a river, locking a 70-credit bond. Its gate is key-bound and stamped with a fable code. Each epoch it files diversion, orchard acreage, and serial. An auditor recomputes diversion from the public river flow table times acreage share; over-claims above 3%, or reused serials, burn the bond. First filing costs 38, kth 38+6(k-1), 1000th 6032; 1000 fake turnouts cost 3,035,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-meter ring fails: serial, fable code, and gauge timestamp must match one turnout. An honest grower pays 38 once and recovers the bond after a clean audit.
